name: Oxidase Test for Bacterial Identification
short_description: SOP for detecting cytochrome c oxidase to differentiate bacterial groups (e.g., Pseudomonas vs. Enterobacteriaceae).
content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: Oxidase Test
## 1. Purpose: Detect cytochrome c oxidase enzyme.
## 2. Specimen: Fresh 18-24h bacterial colony (avoid sugar-containing media like MacConkey).
## 3. Reagents: 1% Tetramethyl-p-phenylenediamine dihydrochloride (Kovacs reagent).
## 4. Procedure:
- Place filter paper on a clean slide.
- Add 1-2 drops of oxidase reagent to the paper.
- Using a wooden stick or platinum loop, rub a heavy inoculum of the colony onto the wet paper.
## 5. Interpretation: Deep purple/blue color within 10-30 seconds = Positive. No color change or >30 seconds = Negative.
## 6. QC: *P. aeruginosa* ATCC 27853 (Positive), *E. coli* ATCC 25922 (Negative).
principle: Cytochrome c oxidase oxidizes the reagent (tetramethyl-p-phenylenediamine) to form a dark purple indophenol compound.

faqs.question: Why avoid nickel/chrome loops for this test?
faqs.answer: Nickel/chrome alloys can cause a false-positive reaction. Use wooden sticks, plastic loops, or platinum.
